description: PH-0.10. This file implements the policy in 13 §16.1 (DEC-59, BR-1826 to BR-1829), which is
the authority — if the two disagree, the document is right and this file is a bug.
`description` is a real Renovate option, valid in the root config and in every packageRule,
and it appears in the PR body where the person reviewing the update will actually read it.
The first version of this file used `_comment` keys instead, which Renovate REJECTS rather
than ignores: it opened a configuration-error issue and did no work at all. Validated by
`pnpm check:renovate` since (BR-1838).

lockFileMaintenance.description: BR-1591 / DEC-46 — exact versions only. A range is how a working build breaks overnight with no code change, so the lockfile is refreshed on the same Monday schedule and never auto-merged.

description: BR-1827 — a security advisory PR is NEVER auto-merged, at any level, however green CI is.
Advisory patches are the class most likely to carry an urgent, lightly-tested change, and
the moment to look closely is not the moment to automate. `schedule: []` lets these escape
the Monday window: waiting five days for a known exploit is worse than an interrupting PR.

packageRules.description: BR-1826 — devDependencies at patch and minor auto-merge on green CI. A devDependency that breaks stops the build loudly and locally; it does not change what the product does in production.
BR-1826 — a devDependency major still changes tooling behaviour. TypeScript, ESLint and Vitest majors have each moved a rule or a default that this repository depends on.
BR-1826 — a runtime dependency is never merged without a human reading the diff, at ANY level. Patch releases have changed runtime behaviour before.
GitHub Actions at patch and minor auto-merge. A workflow that breaks is visible on the next push and affects nothing a user can reach.
A GitHub Actions major can change the runner contract or the inputs. SB-29 — pnpm/action-setup@v4 still targets Node 20, and its successor arrives through this rule.

description: BR-1828 — Docker base images are manual, and this is the rule most likely to be loosened
by someone who does not know why it exists. BR-1810 requires the pinned Node version to
stay identical across engines.node, .nvmrc, packageManager, the CI matrix and every
Dockerfile. Renovate can change the Dockerfile line. Only a person can change all five
coherently, and a bump that moves one of the five is worse than no bump at all, because
the mismatch is silent until something behaves differently in production.
TypeScript is held at 6.0.3 by BR-1805: typescript-eslint declares `typescript: <6.1.0`,
and TypeScript 7 would SILENTLY disable type-aware linting — the mechanism that enforces
BR-1579. The failure mode is a green build with half its rules gone, so this is pinned
here as well as documented. Unpin when typescript-eslint supports TypeScript 7.

packageRules.description: BR-1593 — Node and PostgreSQL track LTS only, so an odd-numbered Node major never appears as a suggestion.
